name: Google (Gmail API)
one_liner: Testing mode works in minutes for up to 100 listed test users, but reading or managing mail uses restricted scopes that need OAuth verification plus a paid annual CASA security assessment before public launch.
difficulty_reason: Almost every useful Gmail scope (readonly, modify, compose, metadata) is restricted, so public launch needs brand verification, scope review with a demo video, and a third-party CASA assessment that you pay for and repeat every year.
time_to_production: about 6 weeks (Google estimate for restricted scopes, not guaranteed) plus CASA assessor scheduling; about 10 business days if you only need gmail.send (sensitive)

approval.required_for: Publishing an External app to production that requests sensitive scopes (for example gmail.send) or restricted scopes (gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.metadata, gmail.insert, gmail.settings.*, https://mail.google.com/). Non-sensitive-only apps do not need verification but may do brand verification to show name and logo.
approval.who_reviews: Google Trust and Safety (OAuth app verification team); security assessment by an App Defense Alliance authorized lab
approval.typical_wait: Google states: brand verification 2-3 business days, sensitive scope verification 10 business days, restricted scope verification 6 weeks, and says these estimates are not guaranteed and vary with developer responsiveness. CASA lab start times are set by the lab (for example Leviathan: start within 2, 10 or 30 days depending on price tier).
approval.cost: Google charges no fee. CASA assessment is paid to the assessor and priced by them. Example (assessor's own page, not Google): Leviathan AL1 from $3,000 (no rush) to $6,000 (priority). Annual repeat.

account_prerequisites: Google account with access to Google Cloud console (create a Google Cloud project)
Separate Google Cloud projects for testing and production (Google OAuth policy)
Homepage hosted on a domain you own that describes the app (not only a login page)
Domain ownership verified in Google Search Console by a project owner or editor
Privacy policy on the same domain as the homepage, linked from homepage and consent screen, disclosing how Google user data is used, stored and shared
Demo video (for example unlisted YouTube) showing the full OAuth flow and scope usage
Budget for an annual CASA security assessment if you request restricted Gmail scopes and store or transmit data on servers
Optional: Google Workspace / Cloud Identity organization if you only need Internal users

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project
steps.detail: Create one project for development/testing and a separate one for production. Only submit the production project for verification.

steps.title: Enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: In APIs and Services, enable the Gmail API for the project.

steps.title: Configure Google Auth Platform branding
steps.detail: Set app name, user support email, logo, homepage URL, privacy policy URL, terms URL and authorized domains. Logo upload triggers brand verification.

steps.title: Set audience: user type and publishing status
steps.detail: Choose External for any Google account (Internal only works for your own Workspace org). Leave publishing status as Testing and add up to 100 test users.

steps.title: Choose the narrowest Gmail scopes
steps.detail: Add scopes under Data Access. Prefer non-sensitive (gmail.labels) or sensitive (gmail.send) where possible. readonly, modify, compose, metadata, insert and https://mail.google.com/ are restricted.

steps.title: Create an OAuth client ID
steps.detail: Create a Web application client and register exact redirect URIs (for Composio custom auth, use the callback URI Composio gives you).

steps.title: Test with test users
steps.detail: Connect test accounts. Expect the unverified-app warning and a 7-day expiry on authorizations and refresh tokens while in Testing.

steps.title: Prepare homepage, privacy policy and domain verification
steps.detail: Publish a homepage and privacy policy on your verified domain, with Limited Use disclosure, and verify the domain in Search Console.

steps.title: Record the demo video and write scope justifications
steps.detail: Show the end-to-end flow including the full English consent screen with the exact scopes requested, and each feature that uses each scope. Explain why narrower scopes will not work.

steps.title: Publish the app and submit for verification
steps.detail: Click Publish app to move to In production, then submit verification in the Verification Center. Reply quickly to Trust and Safety emails.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment (restricted scopes)
steps.detail: When Google tells you to start, engage an App Defense Alliance authorized lab, fix findings, and get the Letter of Validation submitted. Repeat every 12 months.

nuances: Gmail scope tiers per Google: non-sensitive = gmail.labels and add-on current-action scopes; sensitive = gmail.send and add-on current message metadata/readonly; restricted = https://mail.google.com/, gmail.readonly, gmail.compose, gmail.insert, gmail.modify, gmail.metadata, gmail.settings.basic, gmail.settings.sharing.
gmail.compose is restricted even though it sounds like sending only. If you only send mail, gmail.send (sensitive) avoids CASA.
In Testing with External user type, authorizations and refresh tokens expire seven days after consent, unless only openid/email/profile scopes are requested.
Testing mode caps you at 100 test users, and a test user consumes the quota once added.
The unverified-app user cap is 100 new users over the project lifetime and cannot be reset or changed.
Limit of 100 refresh tokens per Google Account per OAuth client ID; issuing more silently invalidates the oldest.
Internal user type skips verification and the user cap but only works for users inside your Workspace/Cloud Identity org, and admins may need to allow restricted Gmail scopes.
Verification of a brand change is valid 7 days; if you do not click Publish branding in that window, status becomes Need to re-verify.

Limited Use rules: no ads use, no sale to data brokers, humans may not read mail without affirmative user agreement except security/legal cases. Using data for AI model training needs explicit consent shown in the demo video.
CASA is annual whether or not the app changed; required assurance level (AL1 or AL2) is set by Google/ADA based on users, scopes and risk, and once at AL2 you stay at AL2.

blockers.blocker: Restricted scope (readonly/modify) needed for an agent that reads mail
blockers.how_to_proceed: Budget for CASA and ~6 weeks; or use Composio managed OAuth; or limit to gmail.send/gmail.labels if the feature allows.

blockers.blocker: Test users disconnect every 7 days in Testing
blockers.how_to_proceed: Expected behavior; publish to production (verified) or use Internal user type for in-org use.
Cap cannot be reset; complete verification for the requested scopes.

blockers.blocker: Homepage or privacy policy not on a verified domain
blockers.how_to_proceed: Host both on the same owned domain and verify it in Google Search Console with a project owner/editor account.
Remove unused scopes, request narrower ones, and rewrite justification with feature-level detail.

agent_can_do: Pick the narrowest Gmail scopes for each agent feature and map them to tiers
Draft the privacy policy section on Google user data and Limited Use disclosure
Draft per-scope justification text for the verification form
Write a demo video script and shot list covering consent screen and each scope
Generate and check redirect URIs and OAuth client config
Build in-app consent notices and a data deletion flow needed for CASA
Run pre-assessment security checks (OWASP ASVS based) on the codebase
you_must_do: Own the Google Cloud project and domain, and verify the domain in Search Console
Click Publish app and submit verification as project owner
Record the demo video using the real app and account
Contract and pay a CASA authorized lab, and sign off remediation
Accept Google API Services User Data Policy and keep project contacts current
Repeat the security assessment every 12 months
composio_note: The Composio Gmail toolkit page shows 'Composio-managed OAuth available', so you can connect users through Composio's own verified Google OAuth app with no client ID, secret, verification or CASA on your side. Bring your own OAuth app (custom auth config with your client ID and secret) when you need your app name on the consent screen, scopes Composio's app does not request, or your own rate-limit quota; then you inherit Google verification and the annual CASA assessment for restricted Gmail scopes.

verification.method: Read official Google Cloud Help, Google for Developers and App Defense Alliance pages listed in sources, plus Composio docs; no provider account created
verified: Testing status limits External apps to 100 test users
Testing authorizations and refresh tokens expire after 7 days unless only openid/email/profile scopes
Unverified apps with sensitive/restricted scopes are capped at 100 new users for the project lifetime

gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.metadata, gmail.insert, gmail.settings.basic, gmail.settings.sharing and https://mail.google.com/ are restricted; gmail.send is sensitive; gmail.labels is non-sensitive
Restricted scopes need an annual security assessment by an authorized lab (CASA, AL1 or AL2)
Google stated estimates: brand 2-3 business days, sensitive 10 business days, restricted 6 weeks, not guaranteed
Google charges no fee for the assessment; cost is agreed between developer and assessor
Brand verification needs homepage and privacy policy on a verified owned domain; demo video needed for sensitive/restricted scopes
Composio offers managed OAuth for the Gmail toolkit
inferred: End-to-end time to production with restricted scopes is likely longer than 6 weeks once CASA lab scheduling and remediation are added
Using only gmail.send plus non-sensitive scopes avoids CASA because CASA applies to restricted scopes only
Composio-managed Gmail connections show Composio's app identity on the consent screen, not yours
could_not_verify: Official CASA price ranges (Google publishes none; only assessor pages such as Leviathan give prices)
Real-world restricted-scope review times beyond Google's 6-week estimate (community reports vary; not used here)
Whether users can still click through 'Advanced' on the unverified app screen for restricted Gmail scopes; Google's help page does not describe it
Exact scopes requested by Composio's managed Gmail OAuth app
corrections: CASA is now described with assurance levels AL1 and AL2, and ADA states both are lab-tested; older advice about a cheap 'Tier 2 self-scan' (often quoted at about $540 from TAC Security) reflects the earlier tier model and may not apply
gmail.compose is restricted, not sensitive; only gmail.send is the sensitive way to send mail
The 7-day refresh token expiry is caused by Testing publishing status, not by verification status; publishing to production removes it
The 100 test-user limit and the 100 unverified-user cap are separate limits; the unverified cap counts over the project lifetime and cannot be reset
Google says there is no Google fee for the security assessment; the cost goes to the third-party lab
